issue_context.title: [BUG] File uploads fail which are > 50 MB
issue_context.body:
**Context:**
- Playwright Version: 1.3.0
- Operating System: Windows
- Node.js version: 12.18.3
- Browser: Chromium

<!-- CLI to auto-capture this info -->
<!-- npx envinfo --preset playwright -->

**Code Snippet**
```javascript
const { chromium } = require("playwright");

(async () => {
  const browser = await chromium.launch();
  const page = await browser.newPage();
  await page.setContent(
    '<input type="file" name="fileToUpload" id="fileToUpload">'
  );
  await page.setInputFiles("input", "path/to/large/file.txt");
  await browser.close();
})();

```

**Describe the bug**
When uploading large file, about 100MB, `page.setInputFiles` fails. With Firefox and Webkit it takes some time but it works.

Increasing cache memory size of the browser at launching with parameters regarding to @dgozman browser error.
I saw [here how to increase cache memory depending of browser used ](https://tipsmake.com/how-to-increase-browser-buffer-size-for-better-performance)
and [playwrith api to set config at browser launching ](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browsertype#browsertypelaunchoptions)

**Testing with Chrome**
It should be something like this : 
```
browser = await chromium.launch({
    args: ['--disk-cache-size=2073741824'], // in bytes = 2Gb
    headless : false,
});
  ```
Chrome is nicely launched with this param and others which seems to be playwright's defaults args : 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5748164/113149058-e3097500-9232-11eb-94fa-f7820c1a34d6.png)

Cache still little... 😭
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5748164/113149212-0e8c5f80-9233-11eb-8528-a1f7c995e59b.png)

**Testing with Firefox**
It should be something like this : 
```
  browser = await firefox.launch({
     headless: false,
     firefoxUserPrefs: {
       'browser.cache.disk.smart_size.enabled': false,
       'browser.cache.disk.capacity' : 2048576, //2gb
     }
   });
  ```
 But still failing as shawn in my previous post whereas when adding a `page.waitForTimeout(xxxx)` I can manualy check the `about:config` and params are goodly set as I wanted... so maybe not a "cache-problem" with firefox... 
 
 
 
 I'm loosing faith... Have you got any idea ? Am I missing something ?

I'm trying to prioritize this, could you share what kind of testing scenario requires uploading 100Mb+ files?

At a high level, I'm working on a system that allows users to submit Docker images as .tar files and get feedback about how well those images work and how they compare to each other. All of our example images, using Python, were too large to upload... we have a workaround using a much smaller image written in Go, but we'd like to automate testing of some 100MB+ files, since that is more realistic: our customers will typically using languages like Python. We want to verify that this software works correctly in a classified environment without direct access to the internet. (I can't share much more of the details of our system.)

In my case, I use it for automating steps on a cloud provider that doesn't give a way to upload on my OS other than by the browser. To make a big range of backup, it's easier with few lines of code than doing it manually.
